parsed.explanation: No trans-specific offence, border rule, facility ban, or documented anti-trans violence/targeting is in the dossier, and enforcement of the morality statute is episodic, not a sweep: 2022 leaked-video prosecution and June-Dec 2024 detention/conviction of two women, with no arrests in 2023. That documented, enforced same-sex criminalisation is secondary for a trans visitor, but it is not a dead letter, penalties are disputed at 6 months to 5 years, government has refused decriminalisation, and stigma, ostracism and non-disclosure are documented with widespread impunity and no recourse. Extrapolating from that thin structural record, an outed visibly nonconforming visitor faces arrest/detention and imprisonment risk plus societal hostility without effective remedy, but not routine universal exposure, organised targeting, torture or execution.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Same-sex morality cases resulted in prosecution in 2022 and June-Dec 2024 detention followed by 5- and 6-month sentences; no trans-specific custody practice documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A presentation or sexual-conduct allegation could be investigated under the morality provision, but no documented trans presentation arrests.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Article 300/318 criminalises same-sex sexual acts contrary to morality, penalty sources range 6 months-5 years; enforced in 2022 and 2024, government repeatedly refused decriminalisation.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Authorities reported no arrests/prosecutions in 2023 and no active enforcement that year; enforcement is case-driven, not systematic.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: For a trans visitor this is a secondary police lever if read as same-sex conduct, notably travelling with a partner, rather than a trans-specific statute.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Stigmatisation, discrimination in education/employment and ostracism from homes/neighbourhoods/villages documented for LGBTQ people generally; no documented violence against a trans person and no trans-specific statistics.
street_violence_police_response.protection: 2023 report recorded police statement they did not incite/tolerate violence against LGBTQI+ people and none reported that year, alongside widespread impunity.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Societal hostility could escalate a confrontation, but trans-specific targeting by police or public is not documented.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No non-discrimination law, no legal gender-marker change, no known LGBTIQ organisation with registration chilled; penalty text and article number unresolved across sources.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Absence of resident recognition machinery is not itself visitor exposure, but thin recourse and impunity mean any arrest or hostility has no documented effective remedy.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower severity than 0.35-A: that anchor has routine, universal border denial under a visitor register with no remedy. Here there is no documented visitor-facing universal exposure or border denial, and enforcement was episodic in 2022 and 2024 with none in 2023. Hence safer than 0.35, though imprisonment is documented.

Less safe than 0.55-B: that anchor is mainly administrative secondary screening, refused admission and slow appeals, without imprisonment for identity. Here a criminal morality statute was actually enforced to 5-6 month sentences, there is documented stigma and widespread impunity, and no functioning remedy is documented.

Materially less safe than 0.75-C: that anchor accepts matching markers, trains officers, provides counsel and compensation for detention. Here entry/document practice is undocumented, no anti-discrimination protection is documented, and the only recent enforcement ended in conviction, leaving the visitor with no documented recourse.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime: no documented trans-specific traveller-facing restriction, but an enforced morality criminalisation, documented LGBTQ stigma/ostracism, no known organisations, government refusal to decriminalise, and widespread impunity. Entry, facilities, care and minors are not documented and cannot be treated as safe. The operative risk is episodic police use of the morality law and societal hostility with thin recourse, not organised targeting or universal exposure. That places the case in Elevated Risk, below administrative-only anchors because imprisonment occurred, and above severe systematic anchors because no trans targeting, custody abuse or lethal pathway is documented.
